content: The text provided appears to be a list of references from a scientific or medical document, formatted in a way that includes citation details such as authors, titles, journal names, publication years, and other bibliographic information. 1. The WHO has published consolidated guidelines on the treatment of drug-resistant tuberculosis, which were accessed on June 1, 2021. These guidelines provide updated recommendations for managing this challenging condition. 2. Updated guidelines on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral therapy initiation, and monitoring were also made available by the WHO and accessed on June 1, 2021. 3. A randomized clinical trial, the TB-HAART study, evaluated the efficacy and safety of initiating antiretroviral therapy one week after starting tuberculosis treatment in patients with CD4 counts below 200 cells/µL. The findings were published in PLoS One in 2015. 4. A study conducted in Tanzania compared early versus delayed initiation of a fixed-dose combination of abacavir, lamivudine, and zidovudine in patients co-infected with HIV and tuberculosis. The results were published in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses in 2009. 5. Research published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2011 examined the outcomes of earlier versus later initiation of antiretroviral therapy in HIV-infected adults with tuberculosis. 6. A multicenter, non-comparative, open-label, randomized trial investigated the use of dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy in patients co-infected with tuberculosis and HIV. The study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2020. 7. A systematic literature review and network meta-analysis compared the efficacy, tolerability, and safety of dolutegravir and efavirenz 400 mg as first-line antiretroviral therapies for HIV. The findings were published in EClinicalMedicine in 2020. 8. Enhanced prophylaxis combined with antiretroviral therapy was studied in patients with advanced HIV infection in Africa. The results, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2017, demonstrated improved outcomes. 9. The CHER randomized trial in South Africa evaluated early time-limited antiretroviral therapy versus deferred therapy in infants infected with HIV. The results were published in The Lancet in 2013. 10. A prospective cohort study conducted in Eswatini assessed the feasibility of initiating antiretroviral therapy under the treat-all policy in routine conditions. The findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 11. The WHO released a guideline on HIV disclosure counseling for children up to 12 years of age, which was accessed on June 1, 2021. 12. Guidance on HIV testing, counseling, and care for adolescents living with HIV was provided by the WHO, with recommendations tailored for public health approaches and policymakers. This document was accessed on June 1, 2021. 13. A study on cryptococcal meningitis in antiretroviral-naive and antiretroviral-experienced patients treated with amphotericin B or fluconazole was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2007. 14. Early antiretroviral therapy was shown to reduce AIDS progression and mortality in individuals with acute opportunistic infections, as demonstrated in a multicenter randomized strategy trial published in PLoS One in 2009. 15. A Cochrane Database systematic review in 2020 examined the treatment of progressive disseminated histoplasmosis in people living with HIV. 16. A 20-year case series and literature review explored the incidence and trends of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome associated with Histoplasma capsulatum in HIV-infected individuals. The findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2020. 17. The WHO issued a policy brief updating recommendations on firstand second-line antiretroviral regimens, which was accessed on June 1, 2021. 18. Updated recommendations on first-line and second-line antiretroviral regimens, post-exposure prophylaxis, and early infant diagnosis of HIV were provided in an interim guideline supplementing the 2016 consolidated guidelines. This document was accessed on June 1, 2021. 19. A study published in the International Journal of Antimicrobial Agents in 2019 investigated the pharmacokinetics of dolutegravir 100 mg once daily when co-administered with rifampicin. 20. The pharmacokinetics of efavirenz 400 mg once daily co-administered with isoniazid and rifampicin in HIV-infected individuals were studied and published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2018. 21. A systematic review and meta-analysis published in PLoS One in 2013 examined the clinical use of HIV integrase inhibitors. 22. A Phase 1 study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of dolutegravir administered twice daily with rifampin or once daily with rifabutin in healthy subjects. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2013. 23. A Phase 1/2 trial investigated the use of once-weekly rifapentine and isoniazid for tuberculosis prevention in patients with HIV taking dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy. The results were published in The Lancet HIV in 2020. 24. A modeling study published in The Lancet HIV in 2019 assessed the risks and benefits of dolutegravir-based antiretroviral regimens in sub-Saharan Africa. 25. The ODYSSEY trial evaluated simplified dolutegravir dosing for children with HIV weighing 20 kg or more. The pharmacokinetic and safety substudies were published in The Lancet HIV in 2020. 26. A study published in AIDS in 2021 examined the pharmacokinetics of tenofovir alafenamide with and without cobicistat in pregnant and postpartum women living with HIV. 27. A single-arm, open-label trial assessed the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of a single-tablet regimen containing elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide in virologically suppressed HIV-infected children. The findings were published in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health in 2017. 28. A study on the acceptability and palatability of low-dose bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide in children with HIV was presented at the International Workshop on HIV Pediatrics in 2020. 29. A Phase 3 study published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016 reported on switching to tenofovir alafenamide co-formulated with elvitegravir, cobicistat, and emtricitabine in HIV-infected patients with renal impairment.
